quarterly_data.signal: Q4 FY2025 results (call): CFO John Wall said total revenue was $1.440 billion for the quarter; non-GAAP operating margin was 45.8% for the quarter and 44.6% for the year; non-GAAP EPS was $1.99 for the quarter and $7.14 for the year; operating cash flow was $553 million in Q4 and $1.729 billion for the full year, and $925 million was used for buybacks in 2025. CEO Anirudh Devgan: 2025 closed with 14% revenue growth and a record backlog 'well ahead of plan, reflecting broad-based portfolio strength and increasing contributions from our AI solutions'; Wall said 'Fourth quarter bookings were exceptionally strong' and 2025 EPS grew 20%.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 revenue $1.440 billion; Q4 non-GAAP operating margin 45.8% (44.6% for the year); non-GAAP EPS $1.99 (Q4) / $7.14 (year); 2025 revenue growth 14%; Q4 operating cash flow $553 million

quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 and Q1 FY2026 outlook given on the call: FY2026 revenue in the range of $5.9 billion to $6 billion, non-GAAP operating margin 44.75% to 45.75%, non-GAAP EPS $8.05 to $8.15, operating cash flow of approximately $2 billion, and about 50% of free cash flow to be used for buybacks. Q1 revenue $1.420 billion to $1.460 billion, non-GAAP operating margin 44% to 45%, non-GAAP EPS $1.89 to $1.95. The outlook assumes export control regulations 'remain substantially similar for the remainder of the year' and excludes the pending acquisition of Hexagon's design and engineering business.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 revenue $5.9 billion to $6 billion; non-GAAP operating margin 44.75% to 45.75%; non-GAAP EPS $8.05 to $8.15; operating cash flow approximately $2 billion; Q1 revenue $1.420 billion to $1.460 billion

quarterly_data.signal: HOW THE 2026 GUIDE IS BUILT: CFO John Wall called it 'prudent and well-calibrated': 'around 67% of 2026 revenue is coming from beginning backlog', recurring revenue is expected to return to 'double digits, kind of low teen growth' with the recurring mix 'around 80% in fiscal '26' (same as 2025). Hardware is a pipeline business with only about 2 quarters visible, so Cadence expects 'a very strong first half for hardware' and is prudent on the second half. China was 12% of revenue in 2024 and 13% in 2025 and is guided at 12% to 13% for 2026, with 'strong bookings growth in the region' but visibility only into the first half. The pending Hexagon design and engineering acquisition (to accelerate physical AI in autonomous vehicles and robotics) carries annualized revenue of 'about $200 million'; if it closed by the end of Q1 'you're probably looking at $150 million revenue for the year', but it is not in the guide. Wall said 2025 incremental margin was 59% and 'there's no near-term ceiling on operating leverage'; he acknowledged the analyst's point that the 2026 guide implies about 51%.
quarterly_data.figure: around 67% of 2026 revenue from beginning backlog; recurring mix around 80%; China 12% to 13% of 2026 revenue; Hexagon D&E about $200 million annualized ($150 million for the year if closed by end of Q1, not in guide); 2025 incremental margin 59%

quarterly_data.signal: HARDWARE (EMULATION) - ANOTHER RECORD YEAR, ANOTHER EXPECTED IN 2026: Devgan said the hardware business 'delivered another record year with over 30 new customers and substantially higher repeat demand from AI and hyperscalers', and '7 out of the top 10 customers in 2025 were Dynamic Duo customers'; 'With a strong backlog entering 2026, we expect this year to be yet another record year for hardware.' He said 'no complex AI chip or any other mobile or automotive chip, any complex chips are not designed without hardware systems', that 'we design our own chips made by TSMC, and we sell full racks', and that big customers buy 'almost every year'. The Z3 system, now in its second year, 'has capacity to design systems of 1 trillion transistors', with a next system to launch 'in a few years'. He said Cadence is 'taking share in hardware' and demand this year versus last year 'is only stronger'.
quarterly_data.figure: over 30 new hardware customers in 2025; 7 out of the top 10 customers were Dynamic Duo customers; Z3 capacity for 1 trillion transistors

quarterly_data.signal: CHIPSTACK AI SUPER AGENT LAUNCHED: 'Last week, we launched ChipStack AI Super Agent, the world's first Agentic AI solution for automating chip design and verification', which 'provides up to 10x productivity improvement for various tasks, including design coding, generating test benches and debugging' and 'has received compelling endorsements from Qualcomm, NVIDIA, Altera and Tenstorrent, among others'. Devgan cited customer results: Samsung '4x productivity' (Samsung U.S. taped out an SF2 design with Cadence Cerebrus AI Studio), Altera '7 to 10x productivity improvement' on RTL writing, and in physical design 'there could be 7%, 10% PPA improvement, 12% in that range' - close to the gain of a node migration. He said agentic flows run '10 or 100 experiments in parallel' versus '3 or 4 or 5' for a manual user, and that Cadence is developing '4 or 5 big agentic flows' (RTL design/verification, front-end, physical implementation, analog/migration, packaging and system design). Cadence Cerebrus, Verisium and Allegro X AI are 'proliferating at scale'.
quarterly_data.figure: ChipStack up to 10x productivity; Samsung 4x; Altera 7 to 10x; 7%, 10% PPA improvement, 12% in physical design; 10 or 100 experiments in parallel vs 3 or 4 or 5

quarterly_data.signal: AI IS NOT DISPLACING EDA - MONETIZATION PLAN: Asked whether customers could use AI to replace EDA tools, Devgan said 'we have seen absolutely no discussion with customers of reducing the usage. On the contrary, all these AI tools are increasing the usage of our tools', because agents 'call our software to get the job done properly'. He said monetization 'takes 2 contract cycles, and I think we are well into that now', and that ChipStack, a new tool category, will be priced 'as like a virtual engineer or agent' on top of more base-tool licenses. CFO John Wall said 'multiyear subscription remains at the core of our business', with 'more usage-based pricing for incremental capacity and AI-driven optimization' via 'card models and token models', plus scoped outcome-oriented service packages; Devgan said 'we are not seeing any change in the duration' of contracts.

DESIGN FOR AI - HYPERSCALERS MOVING TO CUSTOMER-OWNED TOOLING: Devgan said 'We deepened our long-standing partnership with Broadcom through a strategic collaboration to develop pioneering Agentic AI workflows to help design Broadcom's next-generation products' and in Q&A named NVIDIA and Broadcom as AI leaders Cadence has deep partnerships with. 'A marquee hyperscaler embraced the Cadence digital full flow for its first full customer-owned tooling AI chip tape-out', Cadence 'expanded our footprint at a top hyperscaler' in AI-driven synthesis and implementation including 3D-IC, and 'expanded our footprint at multiple marquee hyperscalers across our EDA, hardware, IP and system software solutions'. Devgan said hyperscalers designing their own chips 'is even more firm now than 1 or 2 years ago' and they will move 'starting with ASIC to hybrid COT to COT' because chips now hold multiple chiplets; each hyperscaler runs 'at least 3 major platforms'. He added 'A merchant semi will do fabulous' too; semi customers are 'about 55% of our business' and the semi/system mix 'moves very, very slowly'. Cadence added 25 new digital full flow logos in 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: at least 3 major platforms for each hyperscaler; semi about 55% of business; 25 new digital full flow logos in 2025

quarterly_data.signal: IP - THIRD YEAR OF STRONG GROWTH: 'Our IP business saw strong momentum with revenue growing nearly 25% in 2025', with 'significant expansions and meaningful competitive wins at marquee customers' across 'HBM, UCIe, PCIe, DDR and SerDes titles', and 'particularly strong adoption' of memory IP including LPDDR6 memory IP for next-generation AI workloads. Devgan said starting backlog in IP is strong, 'not just our traditional business with TSMC, which is doing phenomenal, but we have opportunity to engage with the newer foundries', and that 2026 'should be a strong year for IP'. In Q4 Cadence also launched the Tensilica HiFi IQ DSP (up to 8x higher AI performance, more than 25% energy savings) for automotive infotainment, smartphone and home entertainment.

CORE EDA AND SYSTEM DESIGN & ANALYSIS: 'Our core EDA business delivered strong performance with revenue growing 13% in 2025' and 'Our recurring software business reaccelerated to double-digit growth in Q4'. The Spectre circuit simulator 'saw significant growth at leading AI and memory companies'. System Design and Analysis grew 13% in 2025 and was 'like 16% of revenue in '25', held back by tough comps from BETA multiyear deals in Q4 2024 and a deliberate move to annual subscriptions. The Millennium M2000 AI supercomputer featuring NVIDIA Blackwell 'is ramping nicely'; the 3D-IC platform is 'a key enabler for the industry's transition to multichip architectures'; the Reality data center digital twin 'was deployed at several leading hyperscalers and marquee AI companies'; Infineon (Q3) and STMicroelectronics (Q4) adopted Allegro X for PCB design.
quarterly_data.figure: core EDA revenue growing 13% in 2025; System Design and Analysis 13% revenue growth in 2025, 16% of revenue

quarterly_data.signal: FOUNDRY ECOSYSTEM PARTNERSHIPS IN 2025: Devgan said Cadence 'expanded our collaboration with TSMC to power next-gen AI flows on TSMC's N2 and A16 technologies', 'strengthened our engagement with Intel Foundry by officially joining the Intel Foundry Accelerator Design Services Alliance', 'Rapidus made a wide-ranging commitment to our core EDA software portfolio across digital, custom analog and verification solutions', and 'Samsung Foundry expanded its collaboration with Cadence, leveraging our AI-driven design solutions and IP solutions' (Samsung U.S. used Cerebrus AI Studio to tape out an SF2 design). He also noted industry projections that semis 'might hit $1 trillion this year', about 4 years ahead of the old 2030 expectation.
quarterly_data.figure: TSMC N2 and A16 AI flows; Samsung SF2 tape-out; semi industry might hit $1 trillion this year
